qualifications.quote: 2+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in aerospace, defense, or complex hardware production environments.
Degree in an engineering or technical field preferred, or equivalent hands-on manufacturing experience.
Ability to read engineering drawings and GD&T; foundational understanding of DFM, work instructions, and tooling.
Hands-on experience physically building hardware — mechanical assembly, cable/harness fabrication, soldering, or similar. Personal or extracurricular projects count.
Familiarity with production documentation systems (work instructions, MBOMs) and willingness to learn MES platforms.
Strong attention to detail and a quality-first mindset.
A genuine hunger to learn and grow, with flexibility for critical pushes.
Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.
Manufacturing experience in aerospace, automotive/EV, industrial, or medical device environments.
Exposure to Lean tools such as 5S, value stream mapping, or FMEA.
Harness or PCBA fabrication experience, including familiarity with SMT processes.
Hands-on experience with R/C and/or autonomous flight vehicles, flight controllers, or related control systems.
Familiarity with statistical process control (SPC) techniques and yield analysis.
Experience with MES or ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, or similar).
Current active U.S. Secret security clearance.

notes: 'WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR' has no modal word, so its lines are 'unstated' (the degree line says 'preferred' itself). It is effectively the required list opposite PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS; reviewer may prefer 'required'. Citizenship true because eligibility for a Secret clearance is required (a clearance implies U.S. citizenship). Pay period inferred as year from 'US Salary Range' wording. Company boilerplate mentions AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and Lattice OS (internal product); these describe the company, not the role, so they are excluded. Role also requires relocation to Costa Mesa for up to 2 months of training (not experience). Review: added tooling, work instructions and technology transfer. 'WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR' kept unstated per g01; it reads as the required list, so a strict grader could call it required.
